rtx5090-2gpu.description: 2x RTX 5090 (32 GB) layerwise-offload recipe -- the lightweight, broadly-runnable topology for this case.
rtx5090-2gpu.serve_args: --model-type diffusion --warmup-mode server --model-variant fl2va --tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 1 --performance-mode memory --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder,vae --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 20 --enable-torch-compile false
rtx5090-2gpu.notes: Matches docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3.mdx's verified 2xRTX5090/32GB/377GiB-host recipe as-is. The recorded numbers below (612.65s/556.79s/23366MB) were captured 2026-08-07 on minimax-h3-5090-2gpu-v4 from a run that used --dit-offload-prefetch-size 0 instead of 1, chosen at the time because prefetch-size 1 had intermittently deadlocked at 'Loading MiniMaxH3DiTModel ... Run:ai Model Streamer' on a minority of launches. That deadlock's real cause turned out to be unrelated to prefetch-size -- LayerwiseOffloadManager.__init__ clamps prefetch_size to min(max(1, prefetch_size), num_layers), so 0 and 1 are runtime-identical, and the 0-vs-1 correlation was coincidence (page-cache warmth carried over across attempts). The actual root cause: runai_model_streamer issues an unconditional torch.distributed collective (new_group + all_gather_object) inside find_local_ranks() on the first stream_files() call per component per rank, regardless of the is_distributed argument sglang passes (always False here); any per-rank divergence in layerwise-offload load order or timing can call that ad-hoc group out of lockstep and hang. Fixed at the sglang layer in sgl-project/sglang#33969 (monkeypatches find_local_ranks to skip the collective) -- serve_args here now uses the cookbook's prefetch-size 1 since 0 was never actually load-bearing; re-validate this cell once that PR lands to confirm the hang no longer reproduces even under adversarial per-rank timing. Client wall 612.65s, server-reported inference_time_s 556.79, peak_memory_mb 23366 (well under the 32 GB budget). --performance-mode speed excluded: H3's compile path changes numerics, and speed mode's residency assumption does not fit 32 GB without the layerwise knobs above. Single-GPU (num_gpus=1, tp_size=1) at this exact shape (1344x768, 124 frames) OOMs even at resident-layers=20 -- TP2's per-rank activation footprint (measured ~13 GB/rank at 100% util during a real denoise) roughly doubles unsharded on 1 GPU, on top of a 32 GB card already near its edge per the cookbook's own 2-GPU peak (~31.7 GiB/rank); the case is 2-GPU-only until that's independently reworked.
rtx5090-2gpu.policy_exception: Same correctness exception as the default profile (checked 2026-08-07): MiniMax-H3's torch.compile path changes numerical output per the sglang cookbook, so it is excluded regardless of hardware.

b200-2gpu.description: 2x B200 (183 GB), fully resident -- no layerwise offload needed at this memory class.
b200-2gpu.notes: Validated 2026-08-07 on 2 independent fresh 2xB200 devboxes (h3-b200-2gpu-v2 and its predecessor), same request as the rtx5090-2gpu profile. Two back-to-back runs agreed to 2 decimal places: client wall 80.64s/80.63s, server-reported inference_time_s 75.42/75.42, peak_memory_mb 108328/108358 (well under the 183 GB budget -- room to spare, unlike the 32 GB RTX5090 profile which needs the layerwise-offload knobs). ~7.6x faster wall-clock than the rtx5090-2gpu profile on the identical request; expected given B200's raw compute plus the total absence of the 5090 recipe's CPU<->GPU layerwise-transfer tax. See the vllm-omni entry's b200-2gpu profile for the cross-framework comparison on the same hardware.

VALIDATION PENDING (2026-10-10 round): derived, not yet measured on this hardware. MINIMAX_H3_VAE_DECODER_FUSED_NORM=0 (2026-10-10, MI355X, sglang 3831e7e09): the VAE decoder's fused scale-add RMSNorm Triton kernels (#41906) use PTX inline asm (mul.rn.f32, constraint 'f') from sglang/kernels/numerics.py; on ROCm they fail to compile and decode to an all-NaN video. The flag keeps the eager norm path, which computes the same values.

consumer-dlo-compile-20260807.notes: Requires ffmpeg/ffprobe on PATH for MP4 muxing. The request also needs `aspect_ratio` inside extra_params (the recipe's own T2VA example omits it and 422s with 'RuntimeError: t2va requires an explicit aspect_ratio' as written). CONFIRMED HARDWARE-INDEPENDENT 2026-08-07: re-ran this exact profile on 2xB200 (sm100, datacenter Blackwell) -- it segfaults with the identical signature as on RTX 5090 (native segfault, Python trace through torch Dynamo's custom_eval_frame), 1 step into denoising. vllm-omni.reason: Empirically validated 2026-08-07, first on minimax-h3-5090-2gpu-v4 (2x RTX 5090) then on 2xB200: the default (compiled) profile segfaults identically on both GPU classes 1 step into denoising (see command_profiles.default.notes) -- a confirmed hardware-independent vLLM-Omni bug, despite the recipe's own claim that torch.compile is 'not enabled by default on consumer paths.' --enforce-eager avoids that segfault, but on RTX 5090 it fails differently at startup (a diffusion worker process dies before completing its init handshake, surfaced as EOFError) and never completes a request on that GPU class. On 2xB200 the identical --enforce-eager command works cleanly and completes a correct generation -- see command_profiles.b200-2gpu for the validated numbers and the sglang comparison on the same hardware. Net: vLLM-Omni H3 support is real but fragile below the B200 class tested here; RTX 5090 has no working profile for this case in either variant.

default.description: LightX2V's two-GPU MiniMax-H3 preset made resident and compiled: TP2 DiT, world-TP text encoder, tile-parallel VAE decode, FlashAttention 3 (Hopper).

upstream_recipe.section: TP2 preset (scripts/minimax_h3/README.md parallel table: TP2 -> --nproc_per_node 2), served per 'Server and POST' with --model-variant fl2av

default.notes: VALIDATION PENDING (2026-10-08): derived offline from LightX2V main 0c2edc12, never run. Upstream's two-GPU MiniMax-H3 preset is configs/minimax_h3/minimax_h3_tp.json (the README's parallel table runs TP2 under torchrun --nproc_per_node 2), served as scripts/minimax_h3/server/start_server.sh does: --model-variant fl2av loads transformer/, there is no startup --task, and each request names task t2av. Kept from the preset: TP2 DiT, the text encoder tensor-parallel over the world group, resident DiT and text encoder, VAE spatiotemporal tile-parallel decode, sgl-kernel RMSNorm, no feature caching. Deviations from the preset, all for the benchmark's lossless policy: attn_type flash_attn3 in place of sage_attn2 (int8-QK SageAttention, a different numeric class; FA3 is the fastest exact kernel on Hopper); use_compile true (harness default) with rope_type torch_real_rope, the pairing of upstream's compile preset configs/minimax_h3/minimax_h3_compile.json (an eager run should go back to minimax_h3_triton_rope), but warmup false: that preset's startup warmup compiles at 480x480x158 and 544x960x124, and under torch.compile(dynamic=None) the second shape recompiles every block shape-dynamic, so the case's shape would be served by that dynamic graph -- the harness warms at the measured shape instead; use_adaln_cache false (the preset's true is required only with cpu_offload): that cache serves the ~13B-parameter, timestep-only AdaLN projections from an offline artifact built for one schedule, while sglang runs the standard path in this benchmark (its --minimax-h3-adaln-cache-path is off too), and the projections it skips are a bandwidth-bound read of about 24 GiB of weights per step, split across TP ranks (est. 0.1-0.4% of a step); infer_steps 49 (preset: 29): LightX2V counts DiT evaluations on linspace(1, 0, infer_steps + 1), sglang's num_inference_steps 50 counts the points of linspace(1, 0, 50), so both run the same 49 forwards on the same grid, shifted 12 (video) / 3 (audio). size and num_frames come from each request ([768, 1344], 124). Weights: the repo's Diffusers-layout components (sglang reads the native FL2VA/ and Ref2VA/ partitions of the same repo and revision -- the same checkpoint, packaged twice by MiniMax); model_allow_patterns fetches only what LightX2V reads. vae_cpu_offload false (preset: true) on 141+ GB cards. Resident per GPU: DiT ~31 GiB + text encoder <= 31 GiB + VAEs ~10 GiB -- fits H200/B200, not an 80 GB H100. First GPU round: A/B Ulysses2 (parallel {tensor_p_size: 1, seq_p_size: 2, seq_p_attn_type: ulysses}, the topology sglang runs here) against TP2, and vae_use_compile true (compiled VAE blocks, which upstream's non-CUDA presets set) against off. Needs LightX2V >= 9ea22feb (2026-09-10, --model-variant); the installer's default pin 7efd05f8 predates H3, so a round sets LIGHTX2V_INSTALL_SPEC to main.

default.description: ComfyUI master, core nodes only, the model's official workflow with full-precision weights.
default.notes: Official video_minimax_h3_t2v template: the fl2va checkpoint with no frames attached is T2VA, which is also what sglang serves (model_variant defaults to fl2va). Full bf16 DiT in place of the pruned int8_convrot, bf16 Qwen3-VL-32B in place of nvfp4_awq, fp16 video VAE in place of int8_convrot. BasicGuider = no CFG, matching sglang's fixed guidance 1.0; sigma shift 12 / 3 as the case's flow_shift / audio_flow_shift. One GPU: without CFG there is no branch to split. Weights are the full-precision single-file checkpoints ComfyUI loads (Comfy-Org repackaging or the model's own single-file release); the official template's fp8/int8/nvfp4 defaults are swapped out because they are a different numeric class from every other row. Sampler, scheduler and shift follow the official ComfyUI workflow; steps, CFG, size, frames and seed follow the case. Compile on: the core TorchCompileModel node (inductor) goes behind every diffusion-model loader, as the other competitors run compile-on; measured on FLUX.1 / 1xB200 2026-09-25 at 4.89s against 5.94s and 5.77s eager.

blackwell-gpuonly.description: Blackwell: the default graph with every model resident on the GPU (--gpu-only).
blackwell-gpuonly.notes: B200: --gpu-only keeps every model, text encoders included, stored and run on the card; a 183 GB B200 holds the largest graph here (MiniMax-H3: 62 GB DiT + 48 GB Qwen3-VL-32B + VAEs). Placement only, numerics unchanged. Measured 2026-09-25 on 1xB200, FLUX.1 eager, interleaved arms: default 5.94 / 5.77 / 5.79s against --gpu-only 5.56s and --gpu-only --disable-dynamic-vram 5.57s (Qwen-Image-2.1: 3.75 / 3.91 against 3.47 / 3.48) -- every --gpu-only arm below every default arm; disabling dynamic VRAM on top adds nothing, so the simpler flag is kept.

default.notes: Derived 2026-10-08 from FastVideo's T2VA recipe (SP = num_gpus, FSDP DiT, text encoder and VAE offloaded, eager DiT) for a resident server: no offload, `inference_torch_compile` (FastVideo's regional per-block compile, safe on FA2/FA3/FA4), VAE uncompiled so #1930's bitwise tile split runs. #1930/#1807's bit-identical switches are on (exact RoPE/AdaLN/SwiGLU kernels, VAE tile split, fused Ulysses all-to-all) and the output-changing ones off (FP32 round-once H3 fusions, FA4 packed varlen). The DiT stays FSDP-sharded on Hopper: replicated, the 66.3 GB DiT, the resident 66.7 GB Qwen3-VL and the 11 GB of VAEs come to 144 GB, more than a 141 GB H200 holds. FA3 is what FastVideo's FLASH_ATTN loads when FASTVIDEO_FA4=0 and flash_attn_interface imports; without it FastVideo falls back to SDPA silently. Steps: FastVideo counts sigma grid points as sglang does (scheduling_minimax_h3.py: linspace(1, 0, num_inference_steps)), so 50 runs 49 forwards, as on sglang; vLLM-Omni counts evaluations and runs 50 for the same field. The 12/3 shifts come from the checkpoint's scheduler configs: FastVideo rejects a flow_shift for H3. VALIDATION PENDING (2026-10-08): check the log for 'Using FlashAttention-3 backend', that compile happens inside the harness warmups, and A/B against DIFFUSION_BENCH_DISABLE_TORCH_COMPILE=1 (eager, where the exact kernels take over).

_note: vLLM-Omni requests carry extra_params.preencode_mp4=true (2026-10-08): its documented, off-by-default overlap of MP4 encoding with the VAE decode (byte-identical frames), the counterpart of sglang's default streamed encode (#41819). Both engines run their best documented output path. vLLM-Omni gets num_inference_steps 49 (2026-10-08): since vllm-omni #7219 (2026-09-24) it reads N as N model passes on linspace(1, 0, N+1), while sglang, FastVideo and LightX2V's 49 read 50 as 50 sigma grid points, i.e. 49 passes; 49 gives Omni the identical 50-point grid. Earlier H3 rounds ran Omni one pass more.
